description: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.) is a global fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with a worldwide footprint spanning subsidiaries in over 20 countries including Armenia, Barbados, Belgium, Bermuda, Brazil, Canada, China, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK. The company generates 66-71% of its net revenue from international markets, with significant revenue contributions from the United States ($8.7B), China/Hong Kong ($6.2B), Singapore ($3.6B), Taiwan ($3.3B), Japan ($1.8B), and Europe ($1.6B) in FY2024. AMD employs approximately 31,000 people globally and operates through segments including Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded, serving customers across North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe.

description: Amazon.com, Inc. is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Seattle, Washington, with a vast global geographic footprint. Its operations span three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS operates 114 Availability Zones across 36 geographic regions worldwide, serving customers globally. The company employs approximately 1.576 million people (Q4 2025) and has a presence in numerous countries through its e-commerce, cloud computing, digital streaming, and artificial intelligence businesses. Key global initiatives include Project Kuiper (a LEO satellite network with 250+ satellites in space, targeting commercial services in Q3 2026), the Amazon Leo satellite constellation (20+ launches planned in 2026, over 30 in 2027), and Zoox autonomous vehicle operations with 350K+ riders. The company holds significant international investments including Anthropic and Rivian, and has made major acquisitions such as MGM Holdings and One Medical.

description: ASML Holding N.V. is a Dutch multinational public corporation headquartered in Veldhoven, Netherlands, that develops and manufactures photolithography machines for the semiconductor industry. It is the world's leading lithography tool manufacturer with over 90% market share and the sole producer of extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems essential for advanced microchip production. ASML operates in more than 60 locations worldwide, with major hubs in Veldhoven (Netherlands), Silicon Valley (USA), Wilton (USA), and across Asia. The company employs over 44,000 people representing more than 100 nationalities. ASML's revenue is globally diversified: Taiwan (24.7%), China (22.2%), South Korea (21.3%), United States (9.6%), EMEA (3.7%), Japan (1.9%), and Singapore (0.9%). The company is listed on Euronext Amsterdam and NASDAQ under the ticker ASML, with a market capitalization of approximately €539.5 billion as of early 2026.

description: Broadcom Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California, and a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions. The company operates in two segments: Semiconductor Solutions (networking, wireless, storage, broadband, and industrial chips) and Infrastructure Software (mainframe, cybersecurity, enterprise software, and VMware cloud solutions). Broadcom has a vast global geographic footprint, with revenue spanning the Americas, Asia Pacific (including significant contributions from China, Singapore, and Taiwan), and Europe, the Middle East and Africa. In fiscal year 2025, the Americas contributed $18.9 billion, Asia Pacific $35.9 billion, and EMEA $9.1 billion of total net revenue of $63.9 billion. The company has over 33,000 employees worldwide, operates R&D and manufacturing facilities across North America, Asia, and Europe, and serves customers in more than 170 countries. Broadcom trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol AVGO.

description: TSMC is the world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry, headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan, with a dominant global geographic footprint. In 2025, 74.4% of its US$122.42 billion revenue came from the US, 8.6% from China, 7.9% from Taiwan, 3.9% from Japan, 3.3% from EMEA, and 1.8% from other regions. In 2024, geographic revenue split was North America 70%, China 11%, Asia Pacific (ex-China/Japan) 10%, Japan 5%, and EMEA 4%. The company operates advanced fabs in Taiwan, Arizona (USA), Kumamoto (Japan), and Dresden (Germany), with overseas expansion accelerating its global manufacturing presence. TSMC produces over 12,000 different products for customers worldwide, holds ~70% of the global foundry market share, and manufactures 92% of all logic chips at 10nm or smaller nodes.
